name: Value private investments each quarter (fund interests, co-investments, direct holdings and properties)
summary: Each quarter a four-person valuations team sets the fair value of about 300 private holdings that the manager holds for its pension and insurance clients: interests in private funds valued from the general partner's statement, co-investments valued from the lead sponsor's mark, and direct infrastructure, credit and property holdings valued from deal team models or independent appraisals. Each value is checked by staff independent of the deal team, signed off by the valuations manager and approved as a set by a management valuation committee, then released to unit pricing, accounting and performance. The process is slow because general partners report 45 to 90 days after quarter end, so many fund values are rolled forward with market proxies and revised later, and because a small team must challenge models built by senior investment staff before a fixed committee date.

baseline.org_archetype: A provincial not-for-profit asset manager with about 240 staff and $79 billion under management, investing for four public sector clients through pools and segregated accounts, with private assets held through funds, co-investments and direct holdings.
baseline.notes: Unit of work is one holding valued for one quarter end. About 300 holdings a quarter (100 a month on average, as the org file averages quarterly work by month). Most valuation work falls in the eight weeks after each quarter end; year end adds audit support.

unit_of_work: one private holding valued for a quarter
trigger: Quarter end, followed by the arrival of the general partner's statement, the asset's quarterly operating report or an appraisal report for the holding.
end_state: The holding's fair value for the quarter is approved by the valuation committee and released to pool unit pricing, investment accounting and performance, with any later true-up or audit adjustment recorded.

volume.seasonality: All holdings are valued once a quarter, so the work arrives in the eight weeks after March, June, September and December quarter ends; the year-end quarter adds audited statements and audit sampling.

evidence.note: Same as the org file's private_holdings demand driver: about 300 fund interests, co-investments, direct holdings and properties a quarter, averaged per month.

Three senior analysts in the org file; the quarterly valuation is their main work, with the rest going to audit support, policy work and ad hoc requests. Cost from the org file (Job Bank NOC 11101 Toronto wages with a premium for valuation skills, loaded 1.35).
One manager in the org file; reviews every holding and runs the committee package. Share of time is an estimate.
Deal team principals prepare co-investment marks; about 25 co-investments a quarter at one to four hours each.

roles.title: Senior principal, real estate (transactions and asset management)

evidence.note: Real estate principals update property models for about 50 properties and co-investments a quarter and brief appraisers.
Infrastructure and credit direct holdings need full model updates; about 35 a quarter at two to nine hours each.

roles.title: Manager, investment risk oversight (private markets and counterparty)

evidence.note: Second-line challenge of material or judgmental valuations, a leading practice in the FSRA review; share of time is an estimate.
Finance reviews the package for consistency with the books before the committee.
Assumed chair of the management valuation committee; other members (chief risk officer, vice president investment operations) attend the same meeting and are not modelled separately.

systems.name: Private markets investment accounting and monitoring system (commitments, calls, distributions, valuations)
Custodian portal (custody, accounting records, net asset value reports, cash and corporate action notices)
Market data terminals and vendor feeds (prices, indices, reference data)
Document management system and virtual data rooms
Email, video calls and collaboration suite
Investment data warehouse and business intelligence reports

steps.name: Open the quarter's valuation cycle
steps.description: On the first business day after quarter end the private markets system rolls the period forward, carries the last approved value of every holding into the new quarter, loads quarter-end exchange rates and creates a task list showing each holding's type, owning client accounts, last statement date and valuation method.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Quarterly valuation is required by the client policy; system behaviour is typical of a private markets accounting system set up for quarterly valuation, vendor not named.

steps.name: Confirm quarter cash flows, ownership splits and exchange rates
steps.description: The analyst checks that every capital call, distribution and fee for the holding up to quarter end is booked in the private markets system, ties them to custodian cash records, and confirms the split of the holding across client accounts and the exchange rate used, so that the value can be rolled forward or compared later.

error.defect_description: A late capital call or distribution is missed, so the roll-forward or the statement tie-out uses the wrong base.

next.condition: fund interest valued from a general partner statement
direct or co-invested infrastructure or private credit holding
real estate property or real estate co-investment

evidence.note: Cash flow tie-out is the first step of bringing NAV in phase; the holding mix (about 190 fund interests of about 300 holdings) follows the org file's demand driver note and is tier C.

steps.name: General partner issues the quarterly report and capital account statement
steps.description: The general partner posts the fund's quarterly financial statements and the investor's capital account statement on its investor portal or emails them. Valuations waits until the statement arrives or until the internal cut-off date set for the valuation committee package, whichever comes first.
inputs: fund quarterly close at the general partner

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

next.condition: statement not received by the cut-off

evidence.note: The org file states statements arrive 45 to 90 days after quarter end; ILPA asks for annual reports within 90 days. The share received before a cut-off near day 50 is an estimate.

steps.name: Download the statement and key the reported NAV
steps.description: The analyst logs in to the general partner's portal, downloads the PDF statement, files it in the document system and types the reported net asset value, statement date, currency, unfunded commitment and fee and carried interest lines into the private markets system against the right fund interest and client accounts.

error.defect_description: Wrong NAV, statement date, share class or currency keyed from the PDF.

evidence.note: Manual capture from PDF statements was the common practice in 2019 to 2022 for limited partners of this size; time is an estimate.

steps.name: Chase the general partner for the statement or an estimate
steps.description: For a statement that has not arrived, the analyst emails the general partner's investor relations team asking for the expected date and for a preliminary or flash NAV estimate, and notes any reply so the roll-forward can use the best available information.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Contacting the general partner directly is one of the options listed for limited partners.

steps.name: Roll forward the last reported NAV to quarter end
steps.description: The analyst starts from the last reported NAV, adds capital calls and subtracts distributions since that date, then applies the movement of a public market proxy index chosen for the fund's strategy, adjusted for the fund's lower volatility, and converts to Canadian dollars. A general partner estimate replaces the proxy when one was given.

error.defect_description: The proxy index or volatility adjustment misstates the true movement; the gap shows when the statement arrives.

control.basis: The model manager valuation policy on adjusting reported NAV to the measurement date (IPEV Guidelines section 4.2)

evidence.note: IPEV 4.2 requires adjustment when the NAV date differs from the measurement date; the Kroll slides describe the cash flow and index steps.

steps.name: Check the statement for fair value basis and unusual movements
steps.description: The analyst compares the reported NAV with last quarter and with the cash flows, reads the general partner's explanation of valuation changes, checks that the statement date matches quarter end and that carried interest is deducted, and flags any movement above the policy threshold or any sign that the NAV is not fair value based.

error.defect_description: A stale or non fair value NAV passes the check.

control.basis: The model manager Investments Valuation Policy, which client investment policies require the model manager to apply (written policy with documented inputs and review, as recommended by the IPEV Guidelines): evidence that reported NAV is fair value based before it is used (IPEV 4.1)

next.condition: NAV stale or not at fair value, adjust it

evidence.note: IPEV 4.1 and 4.2 list the factors that call for adjustment; ILPA asks GPs to explain valuation changes. Branch shares are estimates.

steps.name: General partner answers the valuation query
steps.description: The general partner's finance or investor relations team replies to the question, for example explaining a large write-up, a change of method, a missing distribution or a fee line, sometimes after a call with the deal team.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Reply times are an estimate; general partners usually answer large limited partners within a week.

steps.name: Prepare the co-investment value from the lead sponsor's mark
steps.description: The private equity principal collects the lead sponsor's quarterly mark and the company's latest results, checks that the security held matches the sponsor's, applies the model manager's ownership share and exchange rate, and writes a short note on the multiple, debt and any change since last quarter.

error.defect_description: Sponsor mark copied without adjusting for a different security, fee or exchange rate.

evidence.note: Co-investment values are commonly based on the sponsor's reported value and checked against a benchmark model (FSRA). Waits and times are estimates.

steps.name: Independently test the co-investment value
steps.description: A valuation analyst recalculates the implied multiple from the company's results, compares it with listed peers and the entry multiple used at purchase, and checks the sponsor's value against the model manager's own proxy model before accepting it or sending questions back to the deal team.

error.defect_description: A weak sponsor mark is accepted.

control.basis: Client investment policy (The insurance client statement of investment policies and procedures): valuations reviewed and approved by qualified personnel independent of those who transact or manage the investment

next.condition: questions back to the deal team

evidence.note: Independent review is required by the client policy; calibration to entry price is in IPEV 2.6. Challenge rate is an estimate.

steps.name: Update the direct investment valuation model
steps.description: The infrastructure or credit principal updates the discounted cash flow model with the asset's quarterly results, revised forecasts from management, current discount rate and exchange rate evidence, recalibrates to the entry price where the asset is recent, and drafts a valuation memo explaining the change from last quarter.

error.defect_description: Stale forecast, unchanged discount rate or a formula error in the model.

evidence.note: IPEV describes discounted cash flow and calibration; OPTrust values such holdings externally at least every three years or annually when significant. Branch share and times are estimates.

steps.name: Independently review the model and inputs
steps.description: A valuation analyst traces the model's revenue and cost inputs to the asset report, compares the discount rate with recent transactions and broker surveys, reruns the sensitivity table and reviews the memo, then accepts the value or returns it to the principal with challenges.

error.defect_description: A model error or optimistic input is missed.

control.basis: Client investment policy (The insurance client statement of investment policies and procedures): valuations reviewed and approved by qualified personnel independent of those who transact or manage the investment

evidence.note: Independent review of internal models is a leading practice in the FSRA review and a client policy requirement. Challenge rate is an estimate.

steps.name: Update the property valuation or brief the appraiser
steps.description: The real estate principal takes the operating partner's quarterly report, updates rent roll, leasing, capital spending and the capitalisation and discount rates in the property model, and, where an external appraisal is scheduled this quarter, sends the appraiser the data pack and answers questions.

error.defect_description: Rent roll or capital rate not updated, or wrong data sent to the appraiser.

evidence.note: Peer policies appraise properties externally on a rolling cycle (annually for significant assets, at least every three years otherwise); the 35% share and times are estimates.

steps.name: Independently review the internal property update
steps.description: A valuation analyst compares the property's capitalisation rate and market rent with recent transactions and broker surveys, checks the change since the last appraisal and accepts the value or returns it to the real estate team with questions.

error.defect_description: An outdated capitalisation rate is accepted.

control.basis: Client investment policy (The insurance client statement of investment policies and procedures): valuations reviewed and approved by qualified personnel independent of those who transact or manage the investment

next.condition: questions back to the real estate team

evidence.note: Independent review requirement; rates are estimates.

steps.name: Independent appraiser prepares the valuation report
steps.description: An accredited appraisal or valuation firm inspects or desk-reviews the asset, builds its own income and comparable sales or transaction analysis, and issues a draft report with a value conclusion for the quarter end.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: The model manager valuation policy: external appraisal or valuation on a rolling cycle for material direct holdings (peer practice: annually for significant assets, at least every three years otherwise)

evidence.note: External valuation cycles and risk-based use of appraisers are documented in peer policies; turnaround time is an estimate.

steps.name: Review the draft appraisal
steps.description: A valuation analyst reads the draft report, checks the rent roll, cash flows and rates against the model manager's data and market evidence, and either accepts the value or sends comments back to the appraiser for a revised draft.

error.defect_description: A factual error in the appraisal is missed.

control.basis: Client investment policy: third-party valuations provided to the model manager must be reviewed and assessed for reasonableness by the model manager

evidence.note: The client policy requires the model manager to review third-party valuations; comment rate is an estimate.

steps.name: Manager reviews and signs off the holding valuation
steps.description: The valuations manager reviews the holding's file: method, inputs, support, change from last quarter and any open questions, applying the policy's materiality thresholds. The manager signs off, sends it back for more support, or flags it as material or judgmental for independent risk review.

error.defect_description: An error passes manager review.

control.basis: The model manager Investments Valuation Policy, which client investment policies require the model manager to apply (written policy with documented inputs and review, as recommended by the IPEV Guidelines): manager review of each holding valuation

next.condition: material or judgmental valuation, send for risk review

evidence.note: Documented review of inputs and conclusions is IPEV better practice; the client policy names the model manager Investments Valuation Policy. Branch shares are estimates.

steps.name: Revise the valuation and its support for reviewer comments
steps.description: The analyst adds the missing support, corrects the input or calculation the reviewer questioned, or obtains a revised figure from the deal team, and updates the valuation file and memo before resubmitting it for review.

error.defect_description: The correction introduces a new error.

evidence.note: Rework loop; times are estimates.

steps.name: Independent risk challenge of material valuations
steps.description: A manager in investment risk oversight reviews material or judgmental valuations, such as large direct holdings or large write-ups, comparing the assumptions with the risk team's own view of the asset and market evidence, and records agreement or a challenge.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: The model manager risk policy: second-line review of material valuations by a risk team separate from the investment team (FSRA leading practice)

evidence.note: Separate risk control team with a channel to senior management; selection share and times are estimates.

steps.name: Add the holding to the valuation committee package
steps.description: The analyst adds the signed-off value to the committee package: the summary table by asset class and client, movement analysis, list of rolled-forward and stale values, external appraisals done this quarter and backtesting of last quarter's estimates against statements received since.

error.defect_description: Summary table does not match the system value.

evidence.note: IPEV recommends backtesting and committee review; package content is common practice.

steps.name: Finance pre-reviews the valuation package
steps.description: The director of investment accounting reads the package before the meeting, checks that the values tie to what will be booked for each pool and client portfolio, and asks about any value that looks out of line with cash flows or the prior quarter.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Per holding share of a three to four hour package read across about 300 holdings; role taken from the org file's process map.

steps.name: Valuation committee approves the quarter's valuations
steps.description: The management valuation committee, chaired by the chief financial officer with the chief risk officer and the head of investment operations, reviews the package, discusses large movements, rolled-forward values and appraisal results, and approves the set or asks for more work on particular holdings.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: The model manager Investments Valuation Policy, which client investment policies require the model manager to apply (written policy with documented inputs and review, as recommended by the IPEV Guidelines): approval by an independent internal valuation committee

evidence.note: Independent committee review is IPEV better practice; chair and membership are assumptions. Touch time is the chair's per holding share of a two hour meeting and a one hour pre-read.

steps.name: Post approved values and release them downstream
steps.description: The analyst marks the value approved in the private markets system, which flows to the warehouse, and emails pool unit pricing, investment accounting and performance that the quarter's approved valuations are released, with the list of rolled-forward values that may later be revised.

error.defect_description: A value is released before approval or with a typing error.

next.condition: value was a roll-forward and the statement is still due
year-end quarter and the auditor samples this holding

evidence.note: Release step and shares are estimates; the true-up share follows the fund branch probabilities.

steps.name: Late general partner statement arrives after approval
steps.description: The general partner's statement for the quarter arrives after the committee approved a rolled-forward value, often 60 to 90 days after quarter end, or later for year-end audited statements.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Org file states statements arrive 45 to 90 days after quarter end; ILPA allows 90 days for annual reports.

steps.name: Compare the late statement with the rolled-forward estimate
steps.description: The analyst keys the late NAV, measures the difference from the approved estimate, records it in the backtesting log, and decides under the policy threshold whether the difference is taken up in next quarter's value or needs an out-of-cycle revision.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

next.condition: difference below threshold, taken up next quarter

evidence.note: Backtesting against later information is IPEV better practice; threshold share is an estimate.

steps.name: Approve an out-of-cycle revision of the value
steps.description: The valuations manager approves a revised value and notifies unit pricing, accounting, performance and client reporting so that prior period figures can be restated or adjusted, logging the revision for the next committee meeting.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: The model manager Investments Valuation Policy, which client investment policies require the model manager to apply (written policy with documented inputs and review, as recommended by the IPEV Guidelines): revisions above threshold approved and reported to the committee

evidence.note: Revision handling is common practice; approver level is an assumption.

steps.name: External auditor selects the holding and requests support
steps.description: At year end the auditor of the pools and of the client funds samples holdings, requests the general partner statements, audited fund financial statements, roll-forward workings, models and appraisal reports, and sends confirmations to general partners.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: Annual audit of the pools' and client funds' financial statements: audit evidence over existence and valuation of private fund interests and direct holdings

evidence.note: Auditors need more than a manager confirmation and test the investor's valuation process; timing is an estimate.

steps.name: Provide audit support for the sampled valuation
steps.description: The analyst assembles the support file, walks the auditor through the method and roll-forward, answers follow-up questions and, if the audited fund statements show a different year-end NAV, agrees an adjustment with the auditor.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Audit support for alternative investments; times and adjustment rate are estimates.

exceptions.name: Statement not received by the cut-off
exceptions.description: The general partner has not reported by the cut-off, so the analyst chases it, rolls the last NAV forward with cash flows and a proxy index, and compares the estimate with the statement when it arrives.

exceptions.name: Query to the general partner
exceptions.description: A large or unexplained movement, a date mismatch or a missing distribution leads to a question to the general partner before the NAV is accepted.

exceptions.name: Deal team valuation challenged
exceptions.description: The valuations team returns a co-investment mark, a direct model or a property update to the deal team with challenges on inputs such as discount or capitalisation rates.

exceptions.name: Draft appraisal sent back for comments
exceptions.description: The analyst finds factual errors or unsupported rates in an appraiser's draft and asks for a revised report.

exceptions.name: Material true-up after approval
exceptions.description: A late statement differs from the approved roll-forward by more than the policy threshold, so the manager approves an out-of-cycle revision that flows to pricing, accounting and client reports.

exceptions.name: Year-end audit sample
exceptions.description: In the December quarter the auditor samples the holding and asks for full support; a few lead to an agreed adjustment.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from quarter end to an approved value for the holding (including later true-ups)
benchmarks.population: Canadian public sector asset managers and pension investment managers valuing private holdings quarterly

evidence.note: Author estimate. A large Canadian peer published quarter results with private values 43 days after quarter end; this smaller manager relies more on general partner statements that arrive 45 to 90 days after quarter end (org file), so its committee is assumed to meet about 50 to 60 days after quarter end, and true-ups run to about 90 days.

benchmarks.population: The national pension fund manager, quarter ended 30 September 2021
ILPA Principles 3.0 recommendation for private fund annual reports including audited statements
OPTrust, an Ontario public sector pension plan, 2021 policy

benchmarks.value: valued at least annually, reviewed at least quarterly
benchmarks.population: The insurance client insurance fund policy for assets managed by the model manager; the national pension fund manager reviews and updates private asset values at least quarterly

evidence.note: The 2019 the insurance client policy already required quarterly fair value estimates.

pain_points.description: General partners report 45 to 90 days after quarter end, so a quarter of holdings are approved on a rolled-forward estimate and revised later, which ripples into unit prices, performance and client reports.

evidence.note: Lag stated in the org file; adjustment practice in IPEV 4.2 and the Kroll slides.

pain_points.description: Statements come as PDFs from dozens of general partner portals in different layouts and are keyed by hand, which costs time at quarter end and lets keying errors through.

evidence.note: Common limited partner practice before data extraction tools spread; ILPA templates aim to standardise content but not delivery.

pain_points.description: Direct holdings are first valued by the deal teams that bought them, so a small valuations team must challenge senior investment staff's models under time pressure.

evidence.note: Independence requirement in the client policy and FSRA leading practice.

pain_points.description: About 300 holdings pass through one manager's review before a fixed committee date, so reviews queue and the package is built in a rush.

evidence.note: Org file headcount of four in valuations against about 300 holdings a quarter.

pain_points.description: Year-end audits ask for audited fund statements that are often not ready, so analysts roll audited figures forward and answer extensive auditor requests.

sources.title: Wages: Financial Analyst (NOC 11101) in the Toronto Region
sources.supports: Toronto hourly wages for NOC 11101: low 27.97, median 41.60, high 73.57 (reference period 2023-2024).

sources.title: IFRS 13 Fair Value Measurement (IFRS Foundation standard page)
sources.supports: Fair value is the price that would be received to sell an asset in an orderly transaction between market participants (an exit price).

assumptions: Holding mix per quarter: about 190 fund interests (63%), 25 private equity co-investments (8%), 35 infrastructure and private credit direct holdings (12%) and 50 real estate properties and co-investments (17%), consistent with the org file's demand driver note; the split is tier C.

The direct infrastructure path uses the infrastructure principal role for both infrastructure and private credit holdings; private credit principals sit in global credit in the org file and do similar work.

A management valuation committee chaired by the chief financial officer, with the chief risk officer and the vice president of investment operations, approves the full set; only the chair's time is modelled, as a per holding share of the meeting. The model manager's actual committee structure was not found in public sources.

Committee and review steps are written per holding: touch minutes are the holding's share of batch work, and waits reflect the fixed committee date, so the simulated spread of cycle times is wider than the real one, where most values are approved on the same day.
The internal cut-off for general partner statements is assumed near day 50 after quarter end; 38% of fund statements miss it, which matches the org file's 45 to 90 day arrival range.

External appraisal or valuation falls on about 35% of property cases and 15% of direct infrastructure and credit cases each quarter, a rolling cycle between annual and three-yearly as in peer policies.
The insurance client investment policy cited is the version on the web page in 2025; the requirements quoted are assumed to have applied in 2019 to 2022 as well, as the org file also assumes.
Loaded costs per hour are taken unchanged from the org file (wage plus variable pay times a 1.35 loading).
The simulation counts the year-end audit sample on 6% of all holdings (about a quarter of holdings in the December quarter); audit hours outside the sample are not modelled.
